summary: Shoppers size a solar generator kit by the job first (phones and laptops, a camping weekend, a refrigerator through an outage, or 240 V home circuits), then by price tier, and only then by how many panel watts come in the box. In the last 60 days EcoFlow's DELTA 4 and TITAN 5000, Anker's SOLIX S5000 and BLUETTI's Apex 200 all launched, and the federal 30% credit that used to make 3 kWh a threshold no longer applies to 2026 purchases. On Black Friday (2026-11-27) most 200 W and larger panel bundles at BLUETTI, Jackery and EcoFlow are pre-orders into January or sold out, so the in-stock kits from Growatt, ALLPOWERS (P1800, S2000) and Nature's Generator win more lines than their test record alone would give them.

axes.label: battery size: how long it runs your things
axes.why: Every guide read on 2026-11-27 sizes by Wh first. Laura Lancaster (Outdoor Life) splits her picks by job: about 300 Wh a day for small electronics, about 600 Wh for a CPAP night, about 2,000 Wh for a refrigerator day, at least 10 kWh a day for a whole home. PopSci (updated 2026-11-05) says under 1,000 Wh keeps electronics charged and 1,000-1,500 Wh is the minimum for multi-day road trips. All six ChatGPT chats opened with 'what do you need to power, and for how long'. OutdoorGearLab (RJ Spurrier, updated 2026-07-23) measured 80-93% of rated Wh as usable AC energy, so rated Wh overstates every kit.

breakpoints.why: Phones-and-laptops class. Outdoor Life puts small electronics at about 300 Wh a day; PopSci's budget pick (Jackery Explorer 300 v2, 288 Wh) and OutdoorGearLab's 'Best Buy for Phones and Laptops' (Jackery Explorer 300, 260 Wh measured) sit here.

First-kit and camping class. PopSci: 1,000 to 1,500 Wh is the minimum for multi-day road trips. ChatGPT's default starter kit is about 1,000 Wh. OutdoorGearLab measured 870-910 Wh usable from four 1 kWh stations.
Refrigerator-for-a-day class. Outdoor Life: a refrigerator needs about 2,000 Wh for a full day. ChatGPT's refrigerator and outage picks are about 2,000 Wh.

Long-outage class (EcoFlow claims 58 h of refrigerator on 3,072 Wh, a maker figure). It was also the 3 kWh floor for the federal Residential Clean Energy Credit, but the IRS page says the credit is not available for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, so it no longer changes a 2026 purchase.

Whole-home class: the 5 kWh units are the ones with 120/240 V output (Anker SOLIX S5000 5,024 Wh, EcoFlow TITAN 5000 5,020 Wh, Jackery 5000 Plus 5,040 Wh). Outdoor Life sets whole-home need at 10 kWh a day or more.

axes.label: what the whole kit costs at checkout
axes.why: ChatGPT told shoppers to check the final checkout price in 4 of 6 chats and split its picks by price ($549.99 battery only, $699.99-$800 bundle, $1,199-$1,429 outage kits, $1,999.99). Price pages are what worked for us: under-$500 drew 29 visits and 13 buy clicks, under-$1,000 home backup 10 visits and 3 clicks. Google suggested no 'under $...' completions for kits (checked 2026-11-27), so the tiers rest on the chats and our traffic.

breakpoints.why: Budget tier reviewers name: PopSci's best budget pick is $299 (Jackery Explorer 300 v2) and OutdoorGearLab's phones-and-laptops Best Buy lists at $289. A kit with a panel under this price is rare.
Our best-performing price page (29 visits, 13 buy clicks since 2026-10-28). Below it kits are 288 Wh; 1 kWh kits start at $493-$575 with our codes.
ChatGPT's condition for its default 1 kWh + 200 W pick ('$699.99 Black Friday 200W bundle', 'around $700-$800 bundle'). EcoFlow lists DELTA 3 panel kits at $679-$819 (all sold out 2026-11-27).
The line between 1 kWh kits and 2 kWh outage kits: 2 kWh kits with 400 W of panels run $1,119.99-$1,649 at maker stores. Our under-$1,000 home backup page drew 10 visits and 3 clicks.
ChatGPT's upper step ($1,999.99). 3 kWh kits and the cheapest 240 V kit (OSCAL PowerMax 6000 + 400 W, $1,969.98) sit just under it.

axes.label: watts of solar panel in the box, against the battery size
axes.why: It decides whether the kit refills in a day. ChatGPT called 100 W bundles 'less useful', 200 W a starter that 'won't refill quickly' and 400 W+ the refrigerator/outage size. Spearhead Spade (updated 2026-11-17) uses a 'rule of five': battery Wh divided by five gives the panel watts. Outdoor Life tested panels and found at best 25% of full-sun output under heavy cloud. Google suggests 'solar generator kit 600w'.

breakpoints.why: PopSci calls 100 W of input 'about the minimum that you'll reasonably want'. It suits 300 Wh kits; on a 1-2 kWh battery it takes several sunny days.
Rule of five for a 1,000 Wh battery (1,024 / 5 = about 205 W, Spearhead Spade).
Rule of five for a 2,000 Wh battery (about 410 W). ChatGPT's refrigerator/outage kits carry 400 W+.
A Google completion ('solar generator kit 600w') and the rule-of-five size for a 3,000 Wh battery. Very few kits ship with this much panel.

axes.label: AC output: what it can run at once and start
axes.why: ChatGPT asked 'will your appliances fit the output limit and startup surge' in 3 of 6 chats and split picks at 1,500 W, 2,000 W and 2,200-2,400 W. Outdoor Life says a refrigerator surges to about 2,000 W at startup and then runs at about 500 W. OutdoorGearLab weights power output at 60% of its score.

breakpoints.why: ChatGPT's 'lower limit' value tier: fine if devices fit, check appliance startup (Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, Anker SOLIX S2000, BLUETTI Pioneer Na).
The norm for 1 kWh stations (EcoFlow DELTA 3, Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2: 1,800 W each on the makers' pages).
The 2 kWh norm (Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max), and above the ~2,000 W refrigerator startup surge Outdoor Life cites.
30 A at 120 V: what a 30 amp RV inlet can draw and the ceiling for a 120 V-only station (EcoFlow DELTA 3000 Gen4, Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus, Nature's Generator L3600).
The 120/240 V split-phase class (Nature's Generator L6000 6,000 W, Jackery 5000 Plus 7,200 W, Nature's Generator Powerhouse Gen 2 7,200 W).

axes.label: 240 V output from one unit
axes.why: Well pumps, dryers and water heaters need 240 V and most kits are 120 V only. Jackery's HomePower 3600 Plus page says two units must be connected 'to power larger appliances such as well pumps and dryers with 240V output'; Growatt's HELIOS 3600 also needs two units. Google completes 'solar generator with 240v outlet' and 'best solar generator with 240v outlet' (read 2026-11-27).

breakpoints.why: A single-unit 120/240 V station (Nature's Generator L6000, Jackery 5000 Plus) runs a 240 V load out of the box. 'Supports 240 V' on the HomePower 3600 Plus or HELIOS 3600 means buying two stations and a hub.

axes.label: 30 amp RV outlet (TT-30) on the station
axes.why: Google completes 'best solar generator for rv' and 'best solar generator for rv 30 amp' (read 2026-11-27). A TT-30 outlet lets an RV shore cord plug straight in, but only a 3,600 W station can supply the full 30 A.

breakpoints.why: Growatt lists 'TT-30 AC & 30A Anderson' for RVs on the INFINITY 2000 PRO, but at 2,400 W that outlet gives 20 A, not 30.
30 A x 120 V. Stations under 3,600 W have the plug but trip before a 30 A RV's full draw.

axes.label: can add an extra battery later
axes.why: ChatGPT raised it in 2 of 6 chats ('future expansion matters (up to 5kWh)' against 'cannot add an expansion battery') and named two 1 kWh picks that cannot expand.

breakpoints.why: EcoFlow DELTA 3 (1-5 kWh) and Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 (to 11 kWh with five 2 kWh packs) expand; ChatGPT says the Anker C1000 Gen 2 and Jackery 1000 v2 do not.
Growatt's INFINITY 2000 PRO is 'expandable up to 6144Wh', but both of its extra batteries show unavailable on Growatt's store on 2026-11-27.

axes.label: charges and runs below freezing
axes.why: PopSci (updated 2026-11-05) has a 'Best for extreme cold' pick, the BLUETTI Pioneer Na, and Google completes 'best solar generator for cold weather' (read 2026-11-27). Outage kits are bought for winter and often live in a garage, cabin or truck.

breakpoints.why: BLUETTI states the sodium-ion Pioneer Na charges at -15 C (5 F) and discharges to -25 C (-13 F). Growatt's '-22 F cold startup' is a start-up claim, not a charging one.

axes.label: weight of the station you carry
axes.why: ChatGPT split camping from outage picks on it (23.8 lb 'easier to carry', about 25 lb default, about 40 lb for the 2,042 Wh outage battery). OutdoorGearLab weights portability at 25% and weighed every unit; PopSci says most stations are 30-60 lb. Google completes 'best portable solar generator kit'.

breakpoints.why: The 1 kWh one-hand carry class: OutdoorGearLab weighed the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at 24.4 lb, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 at 25.0 lb, Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 25.2 lb, EcoFlow Delta 3 at 28.1 lb.
The lightest 2 kWh class: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 at 38.9 lb measured (OutdoorGearLab) against 53.4 lb for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (PopSci's spec).

axes.label: in stock now, or a pre-order
axes.why: My own judgement, no shopper evidence beyond the stores: on 2026-11-27 Jackery marks its 200 W bundles 'Pre-order, ships by Jan. 6', BLUETTI's 200 W panel kits ship Jan 8, 2027 (our records), and every EcoFlow DELTA 3 panel kit shows unavailable. A kit bought for storm season or as a gift that arrives in January is a different purchase.

breakpoints.why: Jackery's 200 W bundles ship by Jan. 6 and its 2000 v2 station by Dec. 11; Growatt's INFINITY 2000 PRO + 2 x 200 W shows available with no pre-order note.

rules: A kit here is one listing that includes a battery station and at least one solar panel; a station sold alone is not a kit. Capacity is the maker's rated Wh. Usable Wh is a named lab's AC measurement (OutdoorGearLab found 80-93% of rated) and the two are never mixed in one column. Output is continuous watts. BLUETTI 'Power Lifting', EcoFlow 'X-Boost' and Growatt 'Watt+' figures are reduced-voltage modes for resistive loads and are not output. '240 V' counts only when one unit makes it; Jackery's HomePower 3600 Plus and Growatt's HELIOS 3600 need two. A TT-30 outlet on a station under 3,600 W does not deliver 30 A. 'Max solar input' in watts is not comparable across makers without the port's voltage and current limits, and a kit's own panels decide recharge time, not that ceiling. Recharge hours are computed at 75-80% of panel rating and labelled as estimates. Prices are read at the maker's US store on the day, with ship dates, because many bundles are pre-orders. The 30% federal credit ended for property placed in service after December 31, 2025 (IRS); pages must not promise it. 'Expandable' is checked against whether the extra battery can actually be bought.
